title: §2.7 / §2.2 (v0.345): an import alias at a chain head silently shadows a same-named enclosing member — the Warning row fires only when the head resolves to a type
body:
**The question.** §2.7 rule 1 ranks import aliases before the chain-head member fallback, and the table's *Warning* row fires when a "chain head resolves to a type while a same-named accessible member exists". A head that resolves to an alias resolves to a **module**, not a type, so `Tx.M()` inside a type declaring a member `Tx`, in a file with `import A.B as Tx;`, reaches the module's `M` with no warning — the same silent preemption the row polices for types.

**Decide.**
1. First: does §2.2's alias-collision list ("a type declared in the file's module") already reach a nested type of the enclosing type? If it does, only the member case remains.
2. Then: does the *Warning* row also fire when the head resolves to an alias? Recommended: yes, one clause, with the same remedy (`this.Tx.M()` for an instance member; the enclosing type's name for a static).

**Why it was not folded into v0.345.** The fix widens the *Warning* row, which proposal 0202 (`docs/proposals/0202-type-position-qualified-head-is-not-a-chain-head.md`, [#7121](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/7121)) edits twice in this train, and the §2.2 question above decides its scope. It is not 0202's issue: 0202 decides the type-position head.

**Reach.** 0 in-tree sites (no test or document program has a member and an import alias of one name at a chain head).
